'''Simon Marcus Catterall''' (born 1964) is an American physicist at [[Syracuse University]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Simon Catterall |url=https://thecollege.syr.edu/people/faculty/catterall-simon/ |website=College of Arts & Sciences at Syracuse University |access-date=25 February 2021 |language=en-us}}</ref> His research involves High Energy Theory, particularly [[Lattice field theory]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Catterall |first1=Simon |last2=Hubisz |first2=Jay |last3=Balachandran |first3=Aiyalam |last4=Schechter |first4=Joe |title=Elementary Particle Physics at Syracuse. Final Report |date=5 January 2013 |page=14 |url=https://www.osti.gov/servlets/purl/1095082 |access-date=25 February 2021 |publisher=Syracuse Univ., NY (United States) |doi=10.2172/1095082 |osti=1095082 |language=English}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Enslin |first1=Rob |title=Physicists Awarded $1.1 Million Grant |url=https://news.syr.edu/blog/2016/06/08/physicists-awarded-1-1-million-grant-92834/ |access-date=25 February 2021 |work=SU News |date=June 8, 2016}}</ref>

He was elected Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2016 for ''For numerous important contributions to computational physics and [[Lattice field theory]] through studies of gravity, technicolor, and especially the lattice formulation of supersymmetric field theories''.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=&unit_id=DCOMP&institution=Syracuse+University |title=APS Fellow Archive |publisher=[[American Physical Society]] |accessdate=April 20, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Droge-Young |first1=Elizabeth |title=Theoretical Physicist Elected American Physical Society Fellow |url=https://news.syr.edu/blog/2016/10/18/theoretical-physicist-elected-american-physical-society-fellow-31222/ |access-date=25 February 2021 |work=SU News |date=October 18, 2016}}</ref>
